canonical_statement: The study compared kidney, cardiovascular, and safety outcomes after initiation of empagliflozin versus DPP-4 inhibitors in adults with type 2 diabetes, including patients with and without baseline CKD.
The weighted analytic cohort included 62,197 new users: 20,279 initiated empagliflozin and 41,918 initiated a DPP-4 inhibitor.

canonical_statement: Safety outcomes included diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycemia, genital mycotic infection, acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, severe urinary tract infection, and urinary tract cancer.
Data came from electronic health records mapped to the PCORnet common data model across 20 large US health systems.

Follow-up began the day after treatment initiation and ended at the first outcome, death, study end, 12 months after the last observed prescription, drug crossover, or 2 years after index, as applicable.
Baseline CKD was defined as eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m².
The study used post-LASSO propensity-score overlap weighting, including prespecified covariates, subgroup variables, and pairwise covariate-by-subgroup interactions.
Propensity models were fitted separately for participants with and without CKD.
After overlap weighting, all absolute standardized mean differences between treatment groups were <0.1.
Weighted incidence rates were calculated per 1,000 person-years and treatment associations were estimated with weighted Cox proportional-hazards models.
For outcomes with death as a competing event, the study used cause-specific proportional-hazards models with censoring at death.
Initiation of a GLP-1 receptor agonist during follow-up was included in Cox models as a time-dependent variable.
The proportional-hazards assumption was evaluated using weighted Schoenfeld residuals.

Sensitivity analyses included 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity-score matching, an intention-to-treat analysis, a 6-month discontinuation censoring analysis, and an analysis excluding follow-up from March 2020 onward.
The supplement provides the ICD-9/ICD-10 and related code lists used to operationalize baseline covariates and outcomes.
The supplement enumerates the covariates included in the propensity models, spanning demographics, clinical measurements, diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, and health-care utilization.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that empagliflozin initiation was associated with lower kidney and cardiovascular outcome risk than DPP-4 inhibitor initiation over a median of just over one year.
The authors stated that the lower-risk association was apparent in participants both with and without known CKD at baseline.
The discussion suggests that the observed benefits may reflect an SGLT2-inhibitor class effect, but the study directly evaluated only empagliflozin versus DPP-4 inhibitors.
Because treatment was not randomized, residual and unmeasured confounding may remain despite extensive propensity-score overlap weighting.
The exposure was based on prescriptions; the study could not confirm medication dispensing or adherence.
Care received outside participating health systems could be missed, although eligibility required evidence of health-system engagement and mortality was supplemented by external linkage.
The timing of eGFR measurements was not standardized, which could affect identification of sustained kidney-function decline.
The study did not define CKD using albuminuria, limiting CKD phenotyping.
Several outcomes relied on diagnosis/procedure codes rather than prospective adjudication, which may reduce outcome specificity.
The study excluded baseline eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² under contemporaneous prescribing constraints, limiting generalizability to more advanced CKD.
The study was funded by the Boehringer Ingelheim & Lilly Diabetes Alliance.
Boehringer Ingelheim was given an opportunity to review the manuscript for scientific and medical accuracy and intellectual-property considerations.
The competing-interest statement reports multiple consulting, grant, advisory, and committee relationships for several authors; other authors reported no competing interests.
